meta.title: PR #1230: feat(loyalty-member-services): member closure lifecycle and multi-membership status evaluation [LP-1230]
meta.subtitle: 49 files, +2828 -197
meta.summary:
**What it does.** Changes `loyalty-member-services`, `loyalty-internal-services`, `@acme/loyalty-common-lib`, `@acme/loyalty-topic-schemas-lib`, and `@acme/gcp-lib` to add the `POST /v1/member/close` endpoint, add `DISABLED` to `MemberStatus` and `member_disabled` to the `member-events` Pub/Sub topic, gate beta cohort re-invitation in `/v1/auth` and `/v1/member/onboard`, and reactivate existing `CLOSED` memberships in place.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph MS["loyalty-member-services"]
    Auth["POST /v1/auth"]
    Onb["POST /v1/member/onboard"]
    Close["POST /v1/member/close"]
  end
  subgraph Stores["CRM & State Stores"]
    HS["HubSpot CRM"]
    FS["Firestore members"]
    Topic["member-events topic"]
  end
  subgraph IS["loyalty-internal-services"]
    WH["hubspot-webhook"]
    Derive["derive-member-status"]
    Cons["Firestore / HubSpot / Braze / TU consumers"]
  end
  Auth & Onb & Close --> HS & FS
  HS --> WH --> Topic
  Derive --> Topic --> Cons
```

Inside `loyalty-member-services`, `close-account/service-handler.ts` updates the HubSpot Membership object to `CLOSED` with `closure_date` and `closure_reason` and patches the Firestore `members` document. `auth/service-handler.ts` and `onboard/service-handler.ts` evaluate `DISABLED` vs `CLOSED` memberships, check `FF_MEMBER_SERVICES_CONFIGURE_BETA_ACTIVE_COHORTS` (`feature-flags.ts`) via `FeatureFlagService.getString` (`packages/gcp-lib`), and call `reactivateExistingMember` on `CLOSED` rejoin. In `@acme/loyalty-common-lib`, `HubSpotService.checkEmailExists` inspects all Membership associations for a Contact and returns `true` only when an associated Membership is `ACTIVE`, `RESTRICTED`, or `DISABLED`.

Inside `loyalty-internal-services`, `MembershipPipeline` maps HubSpot `DISABLED` changes to `member_disabled` domain events, `derive-member-status` short-circuits when HubSpot status is `DISABLED`, and the Firestore, HubSpot, Braze, and Partner Ingestion consumers subscribe to `member_disabled` and manage `closure_date`, `closure_reason`, `reinvited_cohort`, and `reinvited_at`.

**Coverage.** Thirteen lenses ran in sequence in one agent (`correctness`, `adversarial`, `security`, `data`, `contract`, `infra`, `performance`, `tests`, `standards`, `operability`, `docs`, `structure`, `architecture`). No lens was skipped.

A separate verifier subagent (`47fb6fd4-a542-4f27-87d8-039535296f06`) checked all 13 `high` and `medium` findings (`H1`–`H7`, `M1`–`M6`) in a fresh context against the `<head>` working tree and confirmed all 13 (`CONFIRMED`). Zero `high` findings were refuted, zero findings were marked `PLAUSIBLE`, and zero `nit` findings were dropped.

The standards scan checked `AGENTS.md`, `services/loyalty/AGENTS.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/decisions/adr-005-loyalty-program-member-status.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/config-values-guidelines.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/error-handling-pattern.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/logging-and-tracing.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/testing-approach.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/member-status-and-workflow-states.md`, `docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/join-and-onboard.md`, and `docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/beta-switch-over-and-unified-lifecycle.md`.

The review did not inspect the external HubSpot CRM workflow configuration that writes `reinvited_cohort` and `reinvited_at` or the downstream Acme Core ingestion service implementation outside this repository.

infra: ran, 1 finding (1 high, merged with contract)
operability: ran, 1 finding (1 medium, merged with standards)

issues.title: POST /v1/member/close lets a DISABLED member overwrite their ban with CLOSED
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** A permanently banned (`DISABLED`) member holding an unexpired `loyalty_token` JWT can call `POST /v1/member/close` and overwrite their status to `CLOSED` in HubSpot and Firestore, making them eligible to re-onboard.

**Because:** `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/close-account/service-handler.ts:53` checks only `memberDoc.status === MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` before calling `updateMembershipStatus(membership.id, MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED)` at line 70 and `patchDocument` with `status: MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` at line 94.

**Reach:** Every member transitioned to `DISABLED` in HubSpot while their `loyalty_token` JWT remains valid.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Throw `AccessDeniedError` in `close-account/service-handler.ts` when `memberDoc.status === MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED` or when the HubSpot membership has `member_status === "DISABLED"`.

**Check:** Add a unit test in `close-account/service-handler.test.ts` verifying that `execute` rejects with `AccessDeniedError` and performs no HubSpot or Firestore writes when status is `DISABLED`.
issues.reasoning: The solution design (`member-closure-beta-launch.md:260`) specifies returning `403 AccessDeniedError` if `status === "disabled"`, and `close-account/close-account.openapi-spec.ts:56` declares `ACCESS_DENIED`, yet the handler never checks for `DISABLED`. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/close-account/service-handler.ts:53` checks only `memberDoc.status === MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` before calling `updateMembershipStatus(..., MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED)` at line 70 and `patchDocument` with `status: MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` at line 94 without guarding `MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED`.
issues.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["DISABLED member with JWT"] --> B["POST /v1/member/close"]
  B --> C["status === CLOSED check passes"]
  C --> D["HubSpot & Firestore set to CLOSED"]

issues.title: reactivateExistingMember overwrites a DISABLED HubSpot membership with ACTIVE
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** A member who is `DISABLED` in HubSpot CRM and `CLOSED` in Firestore (from pre-PR webhook projection or webhook lag) passes the Firestore re-onboarding gate and overwrites their HubSpot `DISABLED` ban with `ACTIVE`.

**Because:** `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/onboard/service-handler.ts:972-977` fetches the HubSpot membership via `getMembershipByMemberId(memberId)` and calls `updateMembershipStatus(membership.id, toHubSpotMemberStatus(MEMBER_STATUS.ACTIVE))` without inspecting `membership.properties?.member_status`.

**Reach:** Every `CLOSED` Firestore member whose HubSpot Membership record has `member_status === "DISABLED"` when `POST /v1/member/onboard` runs.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Check `fromHubSpotMemberStatus(membership.properties?.member_status) === MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED` in `reactivateExistingMember` before calling `updateMembershipStatus`, repair Firestore to `MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED`, and throw `AccessDeniedError`.

**Check:** Add a test in `onboard/service-handler.test.ts` where Firestore has `status: "CLOSED"` and `getMembershipByMemberId` returns `member_status: "DISABLED"`, asserting `AccessDeniedError` is thrown.
issues.reasoning: At `<base>`, `MembershipPipeline` mapped HubSpot `DISABLED` to `MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` in Firestore (`membership-pipeline.ts:29` in the diff), so existing banned members have `status: "CLOSED"` in Firestore. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/onboard/service-handler.ts:973` calls `updateMembershipStatus(membership.id, toHubSpotMemberStatus(MEMBER_STATUS.ACTIVE))` without checking if `membership.properties?.member_status` is `DISABLED`.
issues.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Firestore CLOSED / HubSpot DISABLED"] --> B["POST /v1/member/onboard"]
  B --> C["reactivateExistingMember"]
  C --> D["HubSpot overwritten to ACTIVE"]

issues.title: derive-member-status reopens voluntarily CLOSED memberships on partner updates
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** A member who voluntarily closes their loyalty account while keeping their Linkt toll account open is reactivated in HubSpot, Firestore, and Braze when a `partner_account_status_changed` event arrives.

**Because:** `services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/derive-member-status/service-handler.ts:103` returns early only when `currentStatus === MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED`, so a `CLOSED` membership proceeds to `deriveStatus(partnerAccountStatus)` at line 110 and publishes `member_activated` at line 128.

**Reach:** Every voluntarily closed member whose linked acme partner account emits `partner_account_status_changed` with `active`, `activeInArrears`, or `suspended`.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Guard `CLOSED` memberships in `derive-member-status/service-handler.ts:103` so partner account status changes do not transition a `CLOSED` member to `ACTIVE` or `RESTRICTED`.

**Check:** Add a test case in `derive-member-status/service-handler.test.ts` with `hubspotStatus: "CLOSED"` and `MOCK_ACTIVE_EVENT` asserting `mockPublishDomainEvent` is not called.
issues.reasoning: Voluntary loyalty closure leaves the customer's Linkt toll account open (`member-closure-beta-launch.md:196`), and `consume-member-account-status-firestore:51` and `consume-member-account-status-hubspot:74` apply `member_activated` while wiping `closure_date`, `closure_reason`, `reinvited_cohort`, and `reinvited_at`. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/derive-member-status/service-handler.ts:103` short-circuits only when `currentStatus === MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED`, so a `CLOSED` membership proceeds to `deriveStatus(partnerAccountStatus)` at line 110 and emits `member_activated` at line 128.
issues.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["partner_account_status_changed"] --> B["derive-member-status"]
  B --> C["currentStatus === CLOSED passes line 103"]
  C --> D["Emits member_activated & reopens member"]

issues.title: HubSpot closure webhook overwrites saved closure_reason in Firestore with null
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** When a member closes their account via `POST /v1/member/close` with a `reason` or a CSA agent sets `closure_reason` in HubSpot, the subsequent HubSpot `member_status = CLOSED` webhook overwrites `closure_reason` in Firestore with `null`.

**Because:** `services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/hubspot-webhook/lib/pipelines/membership/membership-pipeline.ts:256-261` emits `member_closed` and `member_disabled` without `reason`, and `consume-member-account-status-firestore/service-handler.ts:65` writes `closure_reason: reason ?? null` (`null`) to Firestore.

**Reach:** Every closure via `POST /v1/member/close` with a `reason` and every agent-initiated closure or disablement in HubSpot.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Hydrate `closure_reason` in `MembershipPipeline` (`membership-pipeline.ts:95, 256`) so `member_closed` and `member_disabled` events include `reason`, and omit `closure_reason` from `patchDocument` and `updateMembershipStatus` when `reason === undefined`.

**Check:** Add unit tests in `membership-pipeline.test.ts` and `consume-member-account-status-firestore/service-handler.test.ts` verifying `closure_reason` is preserved.
issues.reasoning: In addition, `packages/loyalty-common-lib/src/providers/hubspot/hubspot-service.ts:1776` writes `closure_reason: options?.closureReason ?? ""` on `CLOSED`/`DISABLED` updates, which clears any existing HubSpot `closure_reason` to `""` when `consume-member-account-status-hubspot:78` processes a status event without `reason`. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/hubspot-webhook/lib/pipelines/membership/membership-pipeline.ts:256` omits `reason` from `member_closed` events, causing `services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/consume-member-account-status-firestore/service-handler.ts:65` to overwrite `closure_reason` with `null`.

issues.title: Partner Ingestion misses reactivation and reuses idempotency_key on 2nd close
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** When a closed member re-onboards, Acme Core never receives an `ACTIVE` ingestion update, and if the member closes their account a second time, the second `member_closed` call sends the same `idempotency_key` as the first closure.

**Because:** `consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/models.ts:10-14` and `api-module.ts:787` exclude `member_activated` (the only event emitted when `reactivateExistingMember` updates HubSpot), and `consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/service-handler.ts:124` hashes only `${event.data.memberId}-${partnerAccountId}-${event.eventName}`.

**Reach:** Every closed member who reactivates via `POST /v1/member/onboard`, and every member who closes their account more than once.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Add `member_activated` to `api-module.ts:787`, `models.ts:10`, and `service-handler.ts:69` (mapping it to `ACTIVE`), and include `event.idempotencyKey` in the SHA-256 hash input at `service-handler.ts:124`.

**Check:** Add unit tests in `consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/service-handler.test.ts` verifying `member_activated` sends `status: "ACTIVE"` and two `member_closed` events produce distinct `idempotency_key` values.
issues.reasoning: Contradicts `member-closure-beta-launch.md:135, 343, 356`, which specifies that `consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion` notifies acme on reactivation. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/models.ts:10` and `api-module.ts:787` exclude `member_activated`, and `service-handler.ts:124` hashes only `${event.data.memberId}-${partnerAccountId}-${event.eventName}` so a second closure reuses the same `idempotency_key`.

issues.title: Beta cohort re-invitation is never synced to Firestore and is blocked by auth
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** A closed member re-invited in HubSpot via `reinvited_cohort` and `reinvited_at` cannot re-onboard during beta, while a member with an inactive cohort passes `isMemberReinvitedToActiveCohort` whenever `reinvitedAt > closureDate`.

**Because:** No webhook pipeline syncs `reinvited_cohort` or `reinvited_at` into Firestore (`auth/service-handler.ts:225-226`); `auth/service-handler.ts:94` still runs `checkPreOnboardingAccess` for eligible `CLOSED` members; and `auth/service-handler.ts:230-232` (and `onboard/service-handler.ts:1031-1033`) returns `true` on `reinvitedAt > closureDate` before checking `activeCohorts`.

**Reach:** Every closed member evaluated for beta re-invitation in `/v1/auth` and `/v1/member/onboard`.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Sync `reinvited_cohort` and `reinvited_at` into Firestore, skip `checkPreOnboardingAccess` in `auth/service-handler.ts:94` for eligible `CLOSED` members, and require `reinvited_cohort` to match `activeCohorts`.

**Check:** Add unit tests in `auth/service-handler.test.ts` for a `CLOSED` member with a declined invitation or inactive `reinvited_cohort`.
issues.reasoning: Also note that `close-account/service-handler.ts:62` writes `closure_date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` while `reinvited_at` is an ISO timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`), so lexicographical `reinvitedAt > closureDate` evaluates to `true` on the same UTC date even if the account was closed after `reinvited_at`; normalize both timestamps before comparing. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/auth/service-handler.ts:94` runs `checkPreOnboardingAccess` for eligible `CLOSED` members (blocking on declined invitation or missing audience), no pipeline syncs `reinvited_cohort`/`reinvited_at` to Firestore, and line 230 returns `true` on `reinvitedAt > closureDate` before checking `activeCohorts`.

issues.title: checkEmailExists swallows HubSpot errors as exists:false and 409s on 0-membership contacts
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** A HubSpot error on the association or membership batch read makes `GET /v1/member/check-email` return `{ exists: false }` for `ACTIVE` or `DISABLED` members, and a Contact with zero memberships returns `{ exists: false }` before failing with `409 Conflict` at `POST /v1/member/onboard`.

**Because:** `packages/loyalty-common-lib/src/providers/hubspot/hubspot-service.ts:397-404` and `441-450` catch all errors and leave `allMemberships` empty, which `hubspot-service.ts:464-475` maps to `false`, while `onboard/service-handler.ts:726` calls `createContact`.

**Reach:** Every `GET /v1/member/check-email` call when HubSpot returns 429/5xx, and every HubSpot Contact with zero memberships.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Rethrow errors in `fetchContactMembershipIds` (`hubspot-service.ts:441`) and the membership batch read (`hubspot-service.ts:397`), and either return `exists: true` when a Contact has zero memberships or reuse the existing Contact in `onboard`.

**Check:** Update `hubspot-service.test.ts` so association and membership batch-read failures reject with `HubSpotError` rather than resolving to `false`.
issues.reasoning: Verifier confirmed: `packages/loyalty-common-lib/src/providers/hubspot/hubspot-service.ts:397` and `441` catch batch-read and association errors and fall through to `evaluateMembershipStatusesForEmailCheck` (line 464), which returns `{ exists: false }` whenever `allMemberships` is empty.

issues.title: close-account marks Firestore CLOSED and returns 200 when HubSpot lookup misses
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** When `getMembershipByMemberId(memberId)` returns `undefined` during `POST /v1/member/close`, the handler marks Firestore `CLOSED` and returns `200 OK`, leaving HubSpot, Braze, and Partner Ingestion `ACTIVE` with no retry path.

**Because:** `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/close-account/service-handler.ts:86-101` logs a warning when `membership` is `undefined`, patches Firestore `status: MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` at line 94, and returns `{ success: true }`, which causes any subsequent retry to short-circuit at line 53.

**Reach:** Any `POST /v1/member/close` call where HubSpot search indexing lags or the CRM membership record is missing.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Throw an error (such as `NotFoundError` or `ServiceError`) when `getMembershipByMemberId` returns `undefined` in `close-account/service-handler.ts:86` before patching Firestore.

**Check:** Update `close-account/service-handler.test.ts:107` to assert that a missing HubSpot membership rejects and does not call `mockMembersCollection.patchDocument`.
issues.reasoning: Because HubSpot is not updated when `membership` is `undefined`, no HubSpot webhook fires to emit `member_closed`, and patching Firestore to `CLOSED` blocks retries at line 53. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/close-account/service-handler.ts:86` logs a warning when `membership` is `undefined` and still patches Firestore to `MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED` at line 93, causing subsequent retries to short-circuit at line 53 while HubSpot remains `ACTIVE`.

issues.title: reactivateExistingMember does not update HubSpot Contact or Partner Account
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** When a closed member re-onboards with an updated email, name, `existingBauMember` flag, or `linktAccountStatus`, `reactivateExistingMember` sends the new profile fields to Braze while leaving the HubSpot Contact and Partner Account stale.

**Because:** `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/onboard/service-handler.ts:988-1005` updates Braze with `validatedRequest` fields without updating the HubSpot Contact or Partner Account, and if `membership` is `undefined` at line 979 it still marks Firestore `ACTIVE` while leaving HubSpot `CLOSED`.

**Reach:** Any returning `CLOSED` member whose re-onboarding request changes contact details or partner account status, or whose HubSpot membership lookup misses.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Throw an error if `membership` is missing at `onboard/service-handler.ts:979`, and update the existing HubSpot Contact properties (`email`, `firstname`, `lastname`, `existing_bau_member`) and Partner Account status in `reactivateExistingMember`.

**Check:** Add a unit test in `onboard/service-handler.test.ts` verifying `reactivateExistingMember` updates HubSpot Contact details and throws if `getMembershipByMemberId` returns `undefined`.
issues.reasoning: New onboarding (`onboard/service-handler.ts:716-733`) writes `email`, `firstname`, `lastname`, and `existing_bau_member` to both HubSpot and Braze, whereas `reactivateExistingMember` writes them only to Braze. Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/onboard/service-handler.ts:979` logs a warning when `membership` is missing yet marks Firestore `ACTIVE` at line 1004, and lines 988-1001 update Braze with new request fields without updating the HubSpot Contact or Partner Account.

issues.guide: config-values-guidelines.md — Feature flags vs structured configuration
issues.title: JSON cohort array is stored as a featureflag_ key and logged via getBoolean
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** Storing a JSON string array under `featureflag_loyalty_member_services_configure_beta_active_cohorts` violates the repository's configuration standard and causes `FeatureFlagService.logFlagValues` to log the parameter as `false` on every refresh.

**Because:** `docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/config-values-guidelines.md` and `packages/gcp-lib/src/util/feature-flag-service.ts:20-23` restrict `FeatureFlagService` to boolean `featureflag_*` flags, and `feature-flag-service.ts:145-150` calls `config.getBoolean(key)` on every `featureflag_*` key.

**Reach:** Every Remote Config template refresh in `loyalty-member-services` when `featureflag_loyalty_member_services_configure_beta_active_cohorts` is configured.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Move the active beta cohorts list into `MemberServicesConfig` (`GcpConfig`) validated with a Zod `z.array(z.string())` schema, or handle string parameters in `logFlagValues`.

**Check:** Verify `FeatureFlagService.logFlagValues` does not log non-boolean cohort arrays as `false` and `MemberServicesConfig` validates the cohort list.
issues.reasoning: Verifier confirmed: `packages/gcp-lib/src/util/feature-flag-service.ts:148` calls `config.getBoolean(key)` on every `featureflag_` parameter in `logFlagValues`, evaluating the JSON string array `featureflag_loyalty_member_services_configure_beta_active_cohorts` as `false` and violating the boolean-only contract at lines 20-23.

issues.guide: services/loyalty/AGENTS.md — ADR and Solution Design documentation rules
issues.title: PR contradicts Accepted ADR-005 without superseding it and adds a parallel Accepted doc
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** `adr-005-loyalty-program-member-status.md` (`status: Accepted`) still defines a 3-value `MemberStatus`, while the PR implements 4 values (`DISABLED`) in a new lifecycle doc marked `Accepted` (`last_reviewed: 2026-10-01`).

**Because:** `member-status.ts:13` adds `DISABLED` without a superseding ADR, and `member-closure-beta-launch.md:1-6` adds a fourth lifecycle doc with `status: Accepted` instead of `Draft` and instead of updating existing lifecycle docs in place per `services/loyalty/AGENTS.md`.

**Reach:** Engineers and agents consulting `docs/design/loyalty/decisions/` or `docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/`.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Add an ADR superseding `ADR-005` for the 4-state `MemberStatus` model, set new design frontmatter `status: Draft` with the actual review date until PR approval, and update the existing lifecycle design docs in place.

**Check:** Confirm `ADR-005` links to its superseding ADR and frontmatter fields match `services/loyalty/AGENTS.md`.
issues.reasoning: Existing accepted lifecycle docs (`member-status-and-workflow-states.md`, `join-and-onboard.md`, `beta-switch-over-and-unified-lifecycle.md`) define the same lifecycle flows. Verifier confirmed: `docs/design/loyalty/decisions/adr-005-loyalty-program-member-status.md:52` defines a 3-value `MemberStatus` without a superseding ADR for `DISABLED`, and `docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/member-closure-beta-launch.md:3-5` is added as a separate file with `status: Accepted` and `last_reviewed: 2026-10-01`.

issues.title: Design doc contradicts code on close-account Firestore writes and flag naming
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** Readers following `member-closure-beta-launch.md` get an inaccurate specification of how `POST /v1/member/close` persists state and what the active cohorts flag is named in code and Remote Config.

**Because:** `member-closure-beta-launch.md:34, 84-94, 261-271` states that `POST /v1/member/close` only mutates HubSpot CRM and relies on the Webhook Translator to update Firestore, whereas `close-account/service-handler.ts:94` patches Firestore directly; and lines 291-294 omit `_configure_` from `FF_MEMBER_SERVICES_CONFIGURE_BETA_ACTIVE_COHORTS` (`feature-flags.ts:12-13`).

**Reach:** Operators configuring Firebase Remote Config parameters and engineers maintaining `POST /v1/member/close`.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Align `member-closure-beta-launch.md` and `close-account/service-handler.ts` on whether `POST /v1/member/close` patches Firestore directly, and update lines 291-294 to match `feature-flags.ts:12-13`.

**Check:** Search `member-closure-beta-launch.md` for `beta_active_cohorts` and confirm the constant and key match `services/loyalty/member-services/src/common/feature-flags.ts:12-13`.
issues.reasoning: Verifier confirmed: `docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/member-closure-beta-launch.md:261-271` states `close-account` only mutates HubSpot and relies on webhook fanout for Firestore (contradicting `close-account/service-handler.ts:93`), and lines 291-293 omit `_configure_` from the flag name defined in `feature-flags.ts:12-13`.

issues.title: Reactivation and DISABLED derivation paths lack assertions and branch coverage
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** Regressions in `reactivateExistingMember` (HubSpot, Braze, and Firestore updates) and in `derive-member-status` (`DISABLED` short-circuit) will not fail any test.

**Because:** `onboard/service-handler.test.ts:435-476` omits `hubspot_customer_id` (leaving lines 989-998 of `onboard/service-handler.ts` unexecuted) and asserts no HubSpot, Braze, or Firestore calls, and `derive-member-status/service-handler.test.ts` has no test for `currentStatus === MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED` (`derive-member-status/service-handler.ts:103`).

**Reach:** `onboard/service-handler.ts:963-1019` and `derive-member-status/service-handler.ts:103-111`.
issues.fix:
**Do:** Add `hubspot_customer_id` to the mocked `CLOSED` member in `onboard/service-handler.test.ts:442`, assert the HubSpot, Braze, and Firestore calls, and add a `DISABLED` test to `derive-member-status/service-handler.test.ts`.

**Check:** Confirm that removing `patchDocument` in `reactivateExistingMember` or the `DISABLED` check in `derive-member-status` fails the tests.
issues.reasoning: Specifically, `reactivateExistingMember` calls `updateMembershipStatus`, `batchCreatePolicyAcceptances`, `upsertCommunicationPreference`, `createBrazeMemberProfile`, and `patchDocument` (while skipping `createMember`). Verifier confirmed: `services/loyalty/member-services/test/functions/onboard/service-handler.test.ts:435-476` omits `hubspot_customer_id` and makes no assertions on HubSpot, Braze, or Firestore calls in `reactivateExistingMember`, and `derive-member-status/service-handler.test.ts` has no test case for `DISABLED`.

issues.title: Centralise member lifecycle state transitions and eligibility guards
issues.impact:
**Breaks:** Changing a member status (`DISABLED`, `CLOSED`) requires coordinated edits across 10+ handlers in `member-services` and `internal-services`, and missing one check lets banned members reactivate or partner updates reopen closed accounts.

**Because:** Transition rules and re-onboarding eligibility are open-coded separately across `close-account/service-handler.ts:53`, `onboard/service-handler.ts:328,973`, `auth/service-handler.ts:137`, and `derive-member-status/service-handler.ts:103`.

**Reach:** Every endpoint and consumer in `loyalty-member-services` and `loyalty-internal-services` that transitions `MemberStatus`.
issues.fix:

DATA.title: POST /v1/member/close lets a DISABLED member overwrite their ban with CLOSED
DATA.impact:
Breaks: A permanently banned (DISABLED) member holding an unexpired loyalty_token JWT can call POST /v1/member/close and overwrite their status to CLOSED in HubSpot and Firestore, making them eligible to re-onboard.

Because: services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/close-account/service-handler.ts:53 checks only memberDoc.status === MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED before calling updateMembershipStatus(membership.id, MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED) at line 70 and patchDocument with status: MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED at line 94.

Reach: Every member transitioned to DISABLED in HubSpot while their loyalty_token JWT remains valid.
DATA.fix:
Do: Throw AccessDeniedError in close-account/service-handler.ts when memberDoc.status === MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED or when the HubSpot membership has member_status === "DISABLED".

Check: Add a unit test in close-account/service-handler.test.ts verifying that execute rejects with AccessDeniedError and performs no HubSpot or Firestore writes when status is DISABLED.

The solution design (member-closure-beta-launch.md:260) specifies returning 403 AccessDeniedError if status === "disabled", and close-account/close-account.openapi-spec.ts:56 declares ACCESS_DENIED, yet the handler never checks for DISABLED.

Verifier confirmed: services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/close-account/service-handler.ts:53 checks only memberDoc.status === MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED before calling updateMembershipStatus(..., MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED) at line 70 and patchDocument with status: MEMBER_STATUS.CLOSED at line 94 without guarding MEMBER_STATUS.DISABLED.

"" on CLOSED/DISABLED updates, which clears any existing HubSpot closure_reason to "" when consume-member-account-status-hubspot:78 processes a status event without reason.

DATA.title: Partner Ingestion misses reactivation and reuses idempotency_key on 2nd close
DATA.impact:
Breaks: When a closed member re-onboards, Acme Core never receives an ACTIVE ingestion update, and if the member closes their account a second time, the second member_closed call sends the same idempotency_key as the first closure.

Because: consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/models.ts:10-14 and api-module.ts:787 exclude member_activated (the only event emitted when reactivateExistingMember updates HubSpot), and consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/service-handler.ts:124 hashes only ${event.data.memberId}-${partnerAccountId}-${event.eventName}.

DATA.fix:
Do: Add member_activated to api-module.ts:787, models.ts:10, and service-handler.ts:69 (mapping it to ACTIVE), and include event.idempotencyKey in the SHA-256 hash input at service-handler.ts:124.

Check: Add unit tests in consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/service-handler.test.ts verifying member_activated sends status: "ACTIVE" and two member_closed events produce distinct idempotency_key values.
DATA.reasoning: Contradicts member-closure-beta-launch.md:135, 343, 356, which specifies that consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion notifies acme on reactivation. Verifier confirmed: services/loyalty/internal-services/src/functions/consume-member-onoffboard-partner-ingestion/models.ts:10 and api-module.ts:787 exclude member_activated, and service-handler.ts:124 hashes only ${event.data.memberId}-${partnerAccountId}-${event.eventName} so a second closure reuses the same idempotency_key.

DATA.title: Beta cohort re-invitation is never synced to Firestore and is blocked by auth
DATA.impact:
Breaks: A closed member re-invited in HubSpot via reinvited_cohort and reinvited_at cannot re-onboard during beta, while a member with an inactive cohort passes isMemberReinvitedToActiveCohort whenever reinvitedAt > closureDate.

Because: No webhook pipeline syncs reinvited_cohort or reinvited_at into Firestore (auth/service-handler.ts:225-226); auth/service-handler.ts:94 still runs checkPreOnboardingAccess for eligible CLOSED members; and auth/service-handler.ts:230-232 (and onboard/service-handler.ts:1031-1033) returns true on reinvitedAt > closureDate before checking activeCohorts.

Reach: Every closed member evaluated for beta re-invitation in /v1/auth and /v1/member/onboard.
DATA.fix:
Do: Sync reinvited_cohort and reinvited_at into Firestore, skip checkPreOnboardingAccess in auth/service-handler.ts:94 for eligible CLOSED members, and require reinvited_cohort to match activeCohorts.

Check: Add unit tests in auth/service-handler.test.ts for a CLOSED member with a declined invitation or inactive reinvited_cohort.
DATA.reasoning:
Also note that close-account/service-handler.ts:62 writes closure_date as YYYY-MM-DD while reinvited_at is an ISO timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ), so lexicographical reinvitedAt > closureDate evaluates to true on the same UTC date even if the account was closed after reinvited_at; normalize both timestamps before comparing.

Verifier confirmed: services/loyalty/member-services/src/functions/auth/service-handler.ts:94 runs checkPreOnboardingAccess for eligible CLOSED members (blocking on declined invitation or missing audience), no pipeline syncs reinvited_cohort/reinvited_at to Firestore, and line 230 returns true on reinvitedAt > closureDate before checking activeCohorts.

SUMMARY.html:
What it does

Changes loyalty-member-services, loyalty-internal-services, @acme/loyalty-common-lib, @acme/loyalty-topic-schemas-lib, and @acme/gcp-lib to add the POST /v1/member/close endpoint, add DISABLED to MemberStatus and member_disabled to the member-events Pub/Sub topic, gate beta cohort re-invitation in /v1/auth and /v1/member/onboard, and reactivate existing CLOSED memberships in place.

flowchart LR subgraph MS["loyalty-member-services"] Auth["POST /v1/auth"] Onb["POST /v1/member/onboard"] Close["POST /v1/member/close"] end subgraph Stores["CRM & State Stores"] HS["HubSpot CRM"] FS["Firestore members"] Topic["member-events topic"] end subgraph IS["loyalty-internal-services"] WH["hubspot-webhook"] Derive["derive-member-status"] Cons["Firestore / HubSpot / Braze / TU consumers"] end Auth & Onb & Close --> HS & FS HS --> WH --> Topic Derive --> Topic --> Cons

Inside loyalty-member-services, close-account/service-handler.ts updates the HubSpot Membership object to CLOSED with closure_date and closure_reason and patches the Firestore members document. auth/service-handler.ts and onboard/service-handler.ts evaluate DISABLED vs CLOSED memberships, check FF_MEMBER_SERVICES_CONFIGURE_BETA_ACTIVE_COHORTS (feature-flags.ts) via FeatureFlagService.getString (packages/gcp-lib), and call reactivateExistingMember on CLOSED rejoin.

In @acme/loyalty-common-lib, HubSpotService.checkEmailExists inspects all Membership associations for a Contact and returns true only when an associated Membership is ACTIVE, RESTRICTED, or DISABLED.

Inside loyalty-internal-services, MembershipPipeline maps HubSpot DISABLED changes to member_disabled domain events, derive-member-status short-circuits when HubSpot status is DISABLED, and the Firestore, HubSpot, Braze, and Partner Ingestion consumers subscribe to member_disabled and manage closure_date, closure_reason, reinvited_cohort, and reinvited_at.

Coverage

Thirteen lenses ran in sequence in one agent (correctness, adversarial, security, data, contract, infra, performance, tests, standards, operability, docs, structure, architecture). No lens was skipped.

A separate verifier subagent (47fb6fd4-a542-4f27-87d8-039535296f06) checked all 13 high and medium findings (H1–H7, M1–M6) in a fresh context against the <head> working tree and confirmed all 13 (CONFIRMED). Zero high findings were refuted, zero findings were marked PLAUSIBLE, and zero nit findings were dropped.

The standards scan checked AGENTS.md, services/loyalty/AGENTS.md, docs/design/loyalty/decisions/adr-005-loyalty-program-member-status.md, docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/config-values-guidelines.md, docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/error-handling-pattern.md, docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/logging-and-tracing.md, docs/design/loyalty/engineering-practices/testing-approach.md, docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/member-status-and-workflow-states.md, docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/join-and-onboard.md, and docs/design/loyalty/solution-designs/member-lifecycle/beta-switch-over-and-unified-lifecycle.md.

The review did not inspect the external HubSpot CRM workflow configuration that writes reinvited_cohort and reinvited_at or the downstream Acme Core ingestion service implementation outside this repository.
